items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I think I am going to be in town, why don‟t you come and play with me while I‟m around town.

ctx.x: One of the guys in the band.

Yeah and it made it wonderful for us because I‟m here and he is over there and Katherine has got this big Olympic swimming pool and a cabana and all that and she would invite all these big clubs and National Conference of Christians and Jews and she had [unintelligible] donors of Africa to have their fashion shows over there. items.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: hired Basie and Clark Smith to start a youth band, and that’s where we came in.

ctx.x: Ray Nance, Lionel Hampton. You know what was so wonderful about that it was a black community, and we didn’t all go to the same school, but we all met musically. So with bands, like, you went to some school, I went to Winifred, but we had rehearsals, and then after hours, we met, and that’s how we got to know each other. And to see all of that going on, we had Clark Smith and the Chicago Defender, the newspaper, hired Basie and Clark Smith to start a youth band, and that’s where we came in. My mother was Nat…
